channel.title: NMX Labs: design, AI and marketing
channel.description: New articles from NMX Labs, Gurugram, on branding, AI design tools, advertising and platform growth, plus free games for creatives.

item.title: The “finished brand” is dead (allegedly): Docker, FutureBrand and rebranding for AI
item.description: In one week Docker swapped its box-carrying whale for “Run on Trust” and FutureBrand declared the static identity system over. Strip away the conference talk and there’s a real shift underneath: your brand now has to be readable by machines. Here’s what that means, with a checklist. #advertising #marketing #nmxlabs

item.title: FMCG is walking away from TV. Should you care?
item.description: India’s biggest soap-and-snack advertisers built their brands on the telly. Now the money is heading to phones, creators and shopping apps, in a year when TV can’t even show its ratings. We went through the numbers to see what’s real, and what a smaller brand should do about it. By dentsu’s estimate, digital took 64% of FMCG ad spend in 2025, up from 53%. TV fell from 40% to 29%. #brandstrategy #marketing #nmxlabs

item.title: Everyone hated the John Lewis Christmas ad. The testers loved it. Who’s right?
item.description: Gloria and Pickles got mauled online, comments switched off and all. Then System1 gave it 5.6 stars, John Lewis’s best festive score since 2019. Both things are true, and the gap between them is the most useful lesson in advertising this Christmas. John Lewis’s 2026 Christmas ad, Gloria and Pickles, starring Dame Kristin Scott Thomas, drew a fierce online backlash and had its YouTube comments switched off. #advertising #marketing #nmxlabs

item.title: Blogging is dead. So why are you still reading this?
item.description: Two-thirds of Google searches now end without a click, and AI answers have eaten the “what is” article whole. We went through the studies. Generic blogs are dying. Blogs with a person, a test and an opinion behind them are doing fine, and the difference is learnable. When Google shows an AI summary, people click a normal result 8% of the time instead of 15%, and about 68% of US Google searches now end with no click at all. #socialmediamarketing #seo #nmxlabs

item.title: Why brands are signing up for cricket beyond the biggest matches
item.description: The DP World Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 in Doha has brought another brand into cricket’s commercial frame: Excitel, now the tournament’s Global Sponsor. Its placements go beyond a logo on a boundary board, reaching the pitch mat and the backdrops used for presentations and interviews. The deal is a useful look at why brands keep investing in cricket, and what turns sponsorship visibility into something people may actually remember. #branding #brandidentity #nmxlabs

item.title: Custom brand typefaces in India: why apps commission their own fonts
item.description: Your font is the voice your brand uses on every screen, price tag and ad. In India it also has to speak several scripts and print a rupee sign. We tested ten popular fonts to see how many can, and the answer explains why big brands commission their own. In our test of ten popular Latin fonts, nine had no Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil or Gujarati characters at all, and two (Open Sans and Archivo Black) lacked the ₹ sign. #branding #brandidentity #nmxlabs

item.title: Generative video for D2C ads in 2026: what Veo and Firefly are actually good for, and what Sora’s sh
item.description: A year ago the question was which AI video model looks best. In 2026 the better questions are which one will still exist next quarter, which one your lawyer is comfortable with, and which shots it should never be trusted with. OpenAI closed the Sora app in April 2026 and its video API in September 2026. If your workflow depends on one model, plan for it to disappear. #aidesign #designtools #nmxlabs

item.title: Latest Adobe AI updates, 21 November 2026: what’s live, what’s beta, and what changed since MAX
item.description: Eleven days after MAX, the release notes have caught up with the keynote. Here’s what you can open today, what’s still in beta, what got clearer this week, and whether the Black Friday offer makes sense for an Indian brand team. Live now: Photoshop Relight, Generative Restyle and a Remove tool that catches shadows; Premiere Color Mode; Firefly Edit Object and Quick Actions. #adobe #adobefirefly #nmxlabs

item.title: Canva vs Figma vs Adobe: the AI design war, and which side a brand team should pick
item.description: Canva gave away a professional design suite. Figma started making marketing assets. Adobe is selling “commercially safe” AI. All three are walking into each other’s territory at once. Here’s the map, and how to pick without changing tools every quarter. Canva is moving up to professionals: it relaunched Affinity as a free pro desktop app in October 2025 and builds sites from prompts with Canva Code. #aidesign #designtools #nmxlabs

item.title: Swiggy vs Zomato: the push-notification copy war, and why brand voice beats discounts
item.description: Any food app can match a coupon by lunchtime. Nobody can copy a voice. Here’s how India’s two delivery apps turned the most ignored channel on your phone into a brand asset, where rivals got it badly wrong, and a copy test we ran on real notifications. A discount can be matched the same day. A recognisable voice can’t, which is why India’s biggest food apps treat notifications as a brand channel. #brandstrategy #marketing #nmxlabs

item.title: 10-minute food: Zepto Cafe vs Swiggy Bolt vs Blinkit Bistro, and why only one model is still growing
item.description: In December 2024 every quick-commerce app wanted to deliver hot food in ten minutes. Two years later, kitchens have closed, apps have been shut and one model is quietly growing. The difference wasn’t speed. It was who had to cook. There were two models: apps cooking in their own kitchens (Zepto Cafe, Blinkit Bistro, Swiggy Snacc) and Swiggy Bolt, which speeds up existing restaurants near you. #brandstrategy #marketing #nmxlabs

item.title: Cadbury’s “Not Just a Cadbury Ad”: the AI personalisation campaign that came too early
item.description: Years before every app could clone a voice, Cadbury made Shah Rukh Khan say the names of thousands of neighbourhood shops. It won India’s first Titanium Lion. Taken apart, it’s still the best brief for AI personalisation an Indian brand has written. In 2020 Cadbury Celebrations gave its Diwali ad space to local shops. In 2021 it went further, using machine learning to recreate Shah Rukh Khan’s face and voice so he named individual stores. #aidesign #designtools #nmxlabs

item.title: Adobe MAX 2026 Sneaks: all 10 projects, ranked by how useful they are for brand work
item.description: Sneaks are Adobe’s research previews, and not all of them ship. We went through all ten from this year and sorted them by what they’d actually change for a brand or ad team. Sneaks are research previews; Adobe doesn’t promise any of them will ship. #adobe #adobefirefly #nmxlabs

item.title: Campa Cola’s comeback: how Reliance restarted the cola war on price
item.description: Reliance bought a 1970s cola for about ₹22 crore, put it in a 200 ml bottle at ₹10 and made Coca-Cola and PepsiCo cut prices. The interesting part isn’t the discount. It’s how a price point became the brand. Reliance acquired Campa in 2022 for about ₹22 crore and relaunched it in 2023 with a 200 ml bottle at ₹10, roughly half what rivals charged at the time. #brandstrategy #marketing #nmxlabs

item.title: Why Zomato renamed itself Eternal: the house-of-brands bet behind India’s best-known food app
item.description: In 2025 Zomato Ltd became Eternal Ltd, but the app you open at 11 pm kept its name. A year later the founder handed the group CEO job to the man who runs Blinkit. Both moves tell the same story, and it’s a story about brand architecture. Only the listed company was renamed. Zomato the app and brand stayed exactly as it was, alongside Blinkit, District and Hyperpure. #brandstrategy #marketing #nmxlabs

item.title: The 10-minute war: how Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart are fighting with brand, not just dark stores
item.description: Speed stopped being a differentiator the day everyone promised ten minutes. Here’s what the numbers say about who’s winning India’s quick-commerce race, how each player is trying to be remembered for something else, and what that means if you sell on these apps. Blinkit leads clearly: about 917 million orders in FY26 against roughly 640 million for Zepto and 412 million for Instamart, per Zepto’s own draft prospectus. #brandstrategy #marketing #nmxlabs

item.title: Amul made memes before the internet: what 60 years of topical ads teach brand teams about moment mar
item.description: In March 1966 a hoarding in Bombay showed a little girl dressed as a jockey and a single pun. More than 4,000 ads later, the format has barely changed. Here’s why it still works and how to borrow it without embarrassing your brand. Amul’s first topical ad ran in March 1966: the mascot as a jockey during Bombay’s racing season, with the pun “Thoroughbread”. #brandstrategy #marketing #nmxlabs

item.title: Why CRED made Rahul Dravid smash a car mirror: the against-type casting playbook
item.description: In April 2021, CRED took the calmest man in Indian cricket and had him scream at traffic. The ad became the most talked-about of that IPL. Here’s the psychology behind casting against type, its risks, and how a brand without a celebrity budget can borrow it. CRED’s April 2021 IPL ad cast Rahul Dravid, famous for his calm, as a road-raging “Indiranagar ka gunda”. It was reported as the most viral ad of IPL 2021. #brandstrategy #marketing #nmxlabs

item.title: Adobe MAX 2026: 5 announcements that change how Indian D2C brands make ads
item.description: Most MAX coverage is written for American agencies with big teams. Here’s what this year’s launches mean for a five-person D2C brand in Delhi, Bengaluru or Mumbai that ships ads every week. Adobe spent MAX 2026 on agents: a Creative Agent across Firefly and Creative Cloud, and previews of AI assistants working inside real Photoshop and Premiere files. #designnews #graphicdesign #nmxlabs

item.title: AI in your Meta ads: the “AI info” label, automatic enhancements and what the new terms mean
item.description: Meta now labels AI-made ads, its tools can change your creative after you upload it, and its updated commercial terms put more of the responsibility on you. A practical checklist. Meta applies an “AI info” label to ads made or significantly edited with its own AI tools, and detects some third-party AI through industry signals. #aidesign #designtools #nmxlabs

item.title: WhatsApp Business pricing changed in October. Here’s why Click-to-WhatsApp ads matter more now
item.description: Service replies on the WhatsApp Business Platform are no longer unlimited and free in India. Conversations that start from an ad still come with a 72-hour free window. WhatsApp Business Platform moved to per-message pricing in 2025, and from 1 October 2026 service messages in India are charged beyond a free allowance. #metaads #digitalmarketing #nmxlabs

item.title: Our AI design workflow: where AI earns its place and where we keep it out
item.description: We use AI on almost every project, and on almost no final pixels of a logo or a label. Here’s the exact workflow, step by step, including the checks that catch the mistakes AI makes confidently. A person writes the brief; AI helps explore directions, not decide strategy. #aidesign #designtools #nmxlabs

item.title: Meta’s Andromeda, explained: why your ad creative now does the targeting
item.description: Meta rebuilt the system that decides which ads are even considered for each person. The practical result: ten near-identical ads now behave like one. Andromeda is Meta’s retrieval system: it narrows tens of millions of ads to a few thousand candidates for each person. #metaads #digitalmarketing #nmxlabs

item.title: How we build a Meta ads creative system instead of a batch of ads
item.description: Most brands brief Meta creative one ad at a time. Then they can’t tell why anything worked. This is the system we use to make creative testable, repeatable and cheaper to refresh. Treat Meta creative as a grid of angles, hooks and formats, not a folder of one-off ads. #metaads #digitalmarketing #nmxlabs

item.title: Packaging labels in India: the mandatory details your designer must leave room for
item.description: A beautiful pack that’s missing the unit sale price or the month of manufacture can be held up at a warehouse or a marketplace. Plan the legal text before the artwork. Packs sold at retail must carry the maker or packer, generic name, net quantity, month and year of manufacture, MRP, unit sale price and consumer care details. #branding #brandidentity #nmxlabs

item.title: How much should an Indian startup spend on Meta ads? A budget guide with the maths
item.description: “Start with ₹500 a day” is the most common advice and usually the wrong number. Your budget should come from your cost per sale, not from a round figure. Here’s how to work it out. Work out your maximum affordable cost per acquisition from margin and repeat orders before picking a budget. #metaads #digitalmarketing #nmxlabs

item.title: Trademarking your brand name in India: a founder’s guide to classes, fees and timelines
item.description: You can design a beautiful brand on a name someone else already owns. A trademark search and filing early on costs little compared to a rebrand later. Search before you design: check the IP India database in every class you’ll trade in. #branding #brandidentity #nmxlabs

item.title: AI product photography for D2C brands: what to generate, and what you still need to shoot
item.description: AI can put your product on a beach, a marble counter or a Diwali table in minutes. It can’t be trusted to draw the product itself. Here’s how we split the work. Shoot the product once, properly: clean packshots on plain backgrounds are the raw material for everything AI does later. #aidesign #designtools #nmxlabs

item.title: What goes in brand guidelines, and how to keep them short enough that people use them
item.description: Most brand guidelines are long PDFs nobody opens after launch. Good ones answer the questions your team, freelancers and marketplace managers ask every week. Write guidelines for the people who make things every week, not for the launch presentation. #branding #brandidentity #nmxlabs

item.title: How much does a logo cost in India, and what are you actually paying for?
item.description: Quotes for “a logo” range from a few thousand rupees to several lakhs. The difference is rarely the drawing. It’s everything that happens before and after it. Logo prices differ mainly in research, number of directions, testing and the files you receive, not in drawing time. #branding #brandidentity #nmxlabs

item.title: The startup branding checklist: what to have ready before you launch
item.description: A logo isn’t a brand, but a brand does need more than good intentions. This is the checklist we use with founders to make sure nothing important is missing on launch day. Decide positioning, customer and personality before designing anything. #branding #brandidentity #nmxlabs

item.title: How sharp is your game brain? Free 2-minute games for creatives
item.description: Quick quizzes and games for creative minds: a Daily five, hex hunch, brief roulette and more. Two minutes, no sign-up, keep a streak. #designgames #creativity #nmxlabs

item.title: Play. Create. Challenge. Quizzes and games for designers and marketers
item.description: Spin the wheel, guess the hex code, roll a client brief: two-minute games about design, branding, ads and AI search. Free on labsnmx.com. #graphicdesign #marketing #nmxlabs
